rawOutput.rationale: Teach a two-step membrane model, then check independent explanation and a final recognition check within the same concept cluster.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because hydrophilic heads face water and hydrophobic tails form a barrier to many polar or charged substances.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
completionEvidence: Explain why a phospholipid bilayer blocks some substances and allows others.
State the difference between passive and active transport in a correct example.

activities.label: Membrane model
activities.title: Why membranes are selective
activities.body: Read the model and identify the two structural parts that matter most.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because hydrophilic heads face water and hydrophobic tails form a barrier to many polar or charged substances.

activities.label: Explain it back
activities.title: Explain selective permeability
activities.body: In your own words, explain why the bilayer lets some substances cross more easily than others.
activities.concept: Explain how phospholipid structure creates selective permeability
activities.correctAnswer: The hydrophilic heads face water and the hydrophobic tails create a barrier, so many polar or charged substances cannot pass easily through the membrane.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both parts of the phospholipid and links the tails to the barrier. If needed, add that some substances cross more easily than others.

activities.label: Fix the model
activities.title: Repair the membrane explanation
activities.body: Correct the missing idea in one sentence, then compare it with the model.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The membrane is selective because the whole bilayer is just a general wall that blocks everything equally.
activities.concept: Explain how phospholipid structure creates selective permeability
activities.correctAnswer: Selective permeability comes from the phospholipid heads facing water and the hydrophobic tails forming a barrier that stops many polar or charged substances, not from the membrane being an equal wall.
activities.feedback: The repair should separate the hydrophilic heads from the hydrophobic tails and tie that structure to selective entry. Do not describe the membrane as blocking everything equally.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: Explain transport types
activities.body: Now explain the difference between passive and active transport in your own words.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
activities.feedback: A complete answer must include both the direction of movement and the energy difference. If you want, add one simple example.

activities.label: Quick check
activities.title: Which transport is which
activities.body: Choose the best answer for the example.
choices: A molecule moving from high concentration to low concentration without cellular energy
A molecule moving from low concentration to high concentration using cellular energy
A molecule staying outside the cell because the membrane is always closed
A molecule moving only because the cell is larger than the molecule
activities.correctAnswer: A molecule moving from low concentration to high concentration using cellular energy
activities.feedback: Active transport requires energy and moves against the concentration gradient. The other choice describes movement down the gradient, which is passive transport.

items.essentialIdea: Phospholipid bilayers let small nonpolar molecules pass because hydrophobic tails form a nonpolar interior.

check.title: Phospholipid Barrier
check.prompt: Why can small nonpolar molecules cross a phospholipid bilayer more easily than ions or large polar molecules?
check.referenceAnswer: The bilayer’s hydrophobic interior allows small nonpolar molecules to diffuse through more easily. Ions and large polar molecules are blocked by that nonpolar core.
check.feedback: Correct: the hydrophobic core favors nonpolar passage and resists charged or polar substances.

items.essentialIdea: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy against it.

check.title: Passive vs Active
check.prompt: How do passive transport and active transport differ in energy use and direction relative to the concentration gradient?
check.referenceAnswer: Passive transport moves down the concentration gradient without energy. Active transport requires energy to move substances against the gradient.
check.feedback: Correct: direction and energy use separate the two processes.

recognitionCheck.title: Transport Comparison
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement best describes active transport?
choices: It moves substances against a concentration gradient using energy.
It moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy.
It occurs only through the phospholipid tails of the bilayer.
It always transports only small nonpolar molecules.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: It moves substances against a concentration gradient using energy.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Correct: active transport requires energy and goes against the gradient.
